title: 3D Asset made entirely made with AI - no human input aside from "a pokeball"
author: spacespacespapce
selftext: Working on a 3D modelling tool for high quality editable assets (that you can download as Blender files) and start using right away in games. If you like what you see, I'm looking for early [testers](https://native-blend-app.vercel.app/).

comments.author: darkwingfuck
comments.body: If you want testers, then open testing. Nobody wants to give a vercel app their email when you have nothing to show but a vibecoded landing page and two spheres

replies.author: tilthevoidstaresback
replies.body: People have definitely paid money for a vibe coded app featuring 2 spheres....but those typically have jiggle physics.

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
Fair enough! You're not wrong, there's definitely a lot of 'vibecoded' stuff out there, and I totally get the skepticism about waitlists.


​My bad if it came across like that. I actually tried to bake in the proof on the landing page itself—if you check out the 3D viewer, you can hit 'Show Mesh' to see the wireframe and separate parts.


All those models are made by the tool. Figured showing the actual mesh quality was better than just another screenshot or generic promise.


I'll post another update here when it's ready to test

comments.author: NormandFutz
comments.body: woah thats crazy is it like one of the 500 others that do this?!

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
You're absolutely right to be skeptical, especially with all the hype in this space. I share that frustration. My intention here isn't to just throw another 'magic button' out there.


My goal is to solve the complicated mesh/poor quality problems with existing tools.



What's the single most important thing an AI 3D tool would need to deliver for you to consider it truly 'useful'?

replies.author: Aggressive-Math-9882
replies.body: 3D printable guns for overthrowing our capitalist overlords.

comments.author: MysteriousPepper8908
comments.body: There's a place for it I guess but isn't this just arranging primitives? The torus appears to be clipping into the button and of course there's no actual opening like an actual Pokeball would need to have.

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
Yup it's not perfect, and I'll shed some light on how it's working.

The agent is modelling using tools in Blender, constructing each sphere, adding the ring and button for the pokeball, coloring it, etc.

https://preview.redd.it/3ld6h83hhpxf1.png?width=730&format=png&auto=webp&s=1692ef0ca3a7359918d95e51023a118bf4342b79

replies.author: PM_ME_UR_PIKACHU
replies.body: As someone who doesn't want to do any modeling i think it looks pretty good. Maybe show a sword next or stylized character. If you can make tools like this that could be used as a plug-in directly in tools like unity or unreal I think you can have a product.

replies.body: Piggybacking on this to also point out that if there’s a model even a novice could make and even unwrap in a reasonable amount of time, this would probably be it. It’s a bad example to show off.

replies.body: Is a very inefficient topology and the intersection of parts in the ring and the button against the sphere body, violates the principle of only quads. The amount of vertex is not compatible among the parts.

replies.author: Environmental_Top948
replies.body: I hope to one day be as knowledgeable as you. I'm still a very beginner.

comments.author: susimposter6969
comments.body: This is way too many polygons to be game ready, are there plans for a post processing pass?

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
Yes! The output is
- a blender file so you can tune the materials and meshes further
- an optimized export to use right away (like .glb, etc.)

comments.author: Independent_Sea_6317
comments.body: The black ring around the pokeball is supposed to be inset, right?

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
Yup you're right.


I wanted to show the render because it's still insane to me that a model could fully make something like this autonomously.


Looping in feedback to make the models more accurate and visually appealing is the next step 🙏
